Getting started with dryaddata

Source: vignettes/dryaddata.Rmd
dryaddata.Rmd

dryaddata is a thin, modern R client for the Dryad REST API (v2). It helps you search and retrieve dataset metadata, walk through versions and files, and download content. OAuth2 authentication and a shared on-disk cache are built in.

library(dryaddata)

Production by default

dryaddata is pointed at Dryad’s production deployment out of the box:

dryad_base_url()
#> [1] "https://datadryad.org/api/v2"

To register for OAuth2 credentials (needed for the dryad_download_*() family), follow the setup steps in vignette("downloading", package = "dryaddata").

If you want to experiment without touching production data, dryaddata also supports Dryad’s public sandbox. dryad_use_sandbox() repoints both the API and the OAuth token URLs at the sandbox host; dryad_use_sandbox(FALSE) reverses the change. The helper returns the previous URLs invisibly so you can restore them. Sandbox accounts are independent of production; register separately at https://sandbox.datadryad.org/account.

Anatomy of a list response

Endpoints that return lists (search, datasets, versions, files) all share a common envelope:

hits <- dryad_search(q = "soil", per_page = 5)

names(hits)
#> [1] "metadata" "records"  "data"

hits$metadata$count   # records on this page
hits$metadata$total   # total matches across all pages
head(hits$data[, c("identifier", "title")])
  • metadata holds counts and the raw HAL _links block (self, next, prev, …).
  • records is the untouched list of objects as returned by the API. Useful when you need a nested field like authors or _links.
  • data is a tidy data frame that stacks scalar fields and keeps nested ones as list-columns.

Walking from a DOI to bytes 

ds <- dryad_dataset("doi:10.5061/dryad.j1fd7")
ds$title
ds$abstract

vs <- dryad_dataset_versions(ds$identifier)
latest <- vs$data$id[which.max(vs$data$versionNumber)]

fl <- dryad_version_files(latest)
fl$data[, c("path", "size", "mimeType")]

Downloading a file requires authenticated credentials (see ?dryad_auth). The chunk below only runs when DRYAD_CLIENT_ID and DRYAD_CLIENT_SECRET are set in the build environment.

Pass path = to set the destination file; otherwise the file is cached at dryad_cache_dir(). The example uses tempdir() so the downloaded file is removed when the R session ends.

csv_path <- dryad_download_file(
  fl$data$id[1],
  path = file.path(tempdir(), "first-file.csv")
)
csv_path
